We need to output test class code that covers the test cases described. The existing test class already covers some cases, but we need to incorporate all cases from JSON list, using parameterized tests where appropriate, and also test exception cases.

We must not modify @Before/@After. We can add parameterized tests using @ParameterizedTest and @MethodSource. We'll need to mock findSchemaResourceRoot() behavior maybe using spy? The method getRefSchemaNode uses findSchemaResourceRoot() which returns a JsonSchema. In our current setup, schema is root; findSchemaResourceRoot() likely returns itself (maybe overridden). We can rely on default behavior. For exception cases where findSchemaResourceRoot returns null, we need to create a spy of JsonSchema and stub findSchemaResourceRoot to return null. Since findSchemaResourceRoot is not final, we can use Mockito.spy and when(...).thenReturn(null). Also need to handle case where getSchemaNode returns null: we can create a spy and stub getSchemaNode to return null.

Also need to test IllegalArgumentException for invalid pointer containing "~". That will be thrown by JsonNode.at when pointer is invalid. So we should assertThrows.

We also need to test NullPointerException when ref is null (NPE occurs at ref.startsWith). So assertThrows NullPointerException.

We need to test handleNullNode fallback: we cannot directly access private method, but we can verify that result is missing node (or maybe something else). In our minimal schema, handleNullNode probably returns MissingNode.instance? Not sure. We'll just assertTrue(result.isMissingNode()).

We also need to test behavior when schema has id. In our test we currently have no id. To test id-based stripping, we need to set up a schema with getId returning something. JsonSchema's getId method likely reads from schemaNode's "$id" property. So we can add "$id": "http://example.com/schemas/main" in the JSON. Then getId will return that value. So we can modify the JSON in setup to include $id. That will affect all tests; but some tests rely on no id. However we can still test both by creating separate schema instances for id scenarios.

Simpler: Keep base schema without id for most tests, and for id-specific tests create separate JsonSchema instance with id property. Use a helper method to create schema with given JSON and maybe id.

We'll add a private method createSchema(String json) that builds JsonSchema using same mocking but with given json.

Now implement parameterized test for the many cases in group getRefSchemaNode.

We'll define a static class TestCase with fields ref, expectedNodePath (String) or expectedBehavior (enum). But easier: Use a method source returning Stream<Arguments> where each argument includes ref string, expectedPath (maybe null) and description. For cases expecting original schema node, we can assert that result equals schema.getSchemaNode() (same instance). For cases expecting node at path, we can assert that result.isMissingNode() is false and that result equals schemaNode.at(path). For expected missing node via handleNullNode, we assertTrue(result.isMissingNode()). For NullPointerException case, separate test.

We'll need to compute expected node path based on description.

4. #/components/schemas/Person -> node at "/components/schemas/Person"
5. /missing/path -> node returned by handleNullNode (missing node)

8. #/ -> original schema node (since node.at("/") returns root)

13. # -> original schema node
14. null -> NPE

16. #/missing/node -> handleNullNode (missing node)

a) findSchemaResourceRoot returns null -> NPE
b) getSchemaNode returns null -> NPE
c) invalid~pointer -> IllegalArgumentException

- For cases requiring id, use schemaWithId; else use schemaWithoutId.

Case6 http://example.com/schemas/main -> after stripping id leaves empty -> original.

Case13 # -> original.

Case14 null -> NPE.

Case16 #/missing/node -> missing node fallback.
